fixes.issues: Nagoji is bare-headed with no rust-red turban, and he wears the blue drill coat. In 15.4 and 15.6, the same evening, he is in a rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, so this breaks continuity within the scene. The staging has also moved off the low wall: both men stand down on the drill ground among the musketeers. Nagoji is reaching his hand into a row of lamps instead of only keeping his eyes on them. Dhanaji himself matches his sheet.

fixes.correction: Nagoji stands with his arms crossed, tunic sleeves rolled to just below the elbow as in the neighbouring panels, his RIGHT forearm on top. That right forearm is smooth, unmarked skin: no scar, no brand, no patch, no lines or veins drawn as marks. His LEFT forearm is tucked underneath with its inner side turned against his body, so the brand and the long white scar on the inner left forearm stay completely hidden. His head is turned slightly aside in a small, slow refusal shake, his chin clean-shaven. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: Lannoy on the left in the white high-collared tunic-coat and mundu, pale hair tied with a black ribbon, turned toward Nagoji with a thin smile and an open-handed gesture; Nagoji on the right in rust-red turban, broad red sash, cream tunic and trousers, talwar at the sash, grey at the temples, small flush gold ear stud; the laterite parapet, the cannon behind, and the dusk sky over the inlet with boats, leaving open sky above and between their heads.
fixes.issues: v01 fails continuity on Nagoji's forearms. His arms are crossed with the RIGHT forearm on top, and that right forearm carries a long pink branching, root-like scar; the bible puts a single long thin WHITE scar on the inner LEFT forearm only. The brand-like patch is on the left forearm but sits up by the elbow, not a hand's width above the wrist. In panel 1, the scar is on his left forearm, so the scar would jump arms within the page. The head-shake beat is also not shown; he simply glares with his arms crossed. Everything else works: Lannoy turned to him with a thin smile and an open-hand gesture, Nagoji's grey temples, flush stud, clean chin, the dusk parapet, the cannon, and plenty of sky for the three lines.

fixes.correction: Nagoji leans forward with both forearms resting on the laterite parapet, tunic sleeves rolled to just below the elbow as in the neighbouring panels. His RIGHT forearm, the one nearest the viewer, is smooth, unmarked skin: no brand, no scar, no patch, no pale lines. His LEFT forearm lies on the far side behind it, inner face down on the stone, so the brand and the long white scar on the inner left forearm are completely out of sight. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: Nagoji in profile facing the water in rust-red turban, broad red sash, cream tunic and trousers and boots, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud; Lannoy standing just behind him on the left in the white high-collared tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, pale hair tied with a black ribbon, hands behind his back, eyes on the water; the cannon on the right, the dusk sky with a low sun over the inlet and sailing boats, and open sky across the top of the frame.
fixes.issues: v01 puts the brand on the wrong arm. Nagoji faces right, so the forearm nearest the viewer is his RIGHT forearm. It clearly shows the puckered brand patch and a long white scar on its outer surface. The bible places both on the inner LEFT forearm, and page 16 panel 1 shows the scar on his left forearm. Otherwise the panel is good: Nagoji leans on the parapet with grey temples, a flush gold stud, a clean chin and a thick moustache; Lannoy stands beside him in white with his eyes on the water; hands and feet are sound; there is no text; and the sky at top centre and right has room for both lines.

fixes.correction: The object Lannoy has thrown must be the same small, irregular, solid grey stone chip he held in the previous panel, a rough flake of laterite with no hole, ring, loop or metal of any kind. It is NOT a chain link, ring, shackle or coin. Show it small and mid-flight, high and well out beyond the parapet over the dark open water, at the top of a long arc, with at most a faint curved motion trail. Lannoy's throwing arm is still fully extended forward and slightly raised after the release, hand open with the fingers spread. Nagoji's eyes and head are turned toward the stone out over the water, following its fall. Keep everything else: the dusk sky and sunset on the inlet, the laterite parapet and cannon, the lit brazier at left, Lannoy's white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals and black hair ribbon, and Nagoji's rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, talwar, clean chin and gold ear stud. Keep open sky at the top for two balloons.
fixes.issues: The thrown object is a dark iron chain link (an oval ring with a hole), not the stone chip from 17.1. That breaks prop continuity and adds an unintended shackle symbol. It also drops straight down just past his fingertips instead of arcing out over the water. Everything else works: both men match their sheets, the dusk and brazier match the bastion, and Nagoji has his clean chin and gold stud.

fixes.correction: Remove the wall map entirely: no maps, charts, printed sheets, posters or framed pictures of any kind anywhere in the room. Where the map hung, show a bare, cold grey whitewashed plaster wall, with at most a small plain wooden crucifix. The upper wall also gives low-detail space for two lettering captions above the boy's head. Keep everything else exactly as before: the pale-haired Flemish boy of about ten in a dark blue wool jacket, brown waistcoat and white cravat, drawing a star-shaped fortress with brass compasses and a wooden ruler on a plain sheet with no people and no writing, the leaded window with a grey northern townscape and church spire, the pewter jug, the inkwell and instrument box, the old books, the empty wooden desks and the coat pegs, all in cold grey light.
fixes.issues: Anachronism. The wall map is a modern map of the Netherlands and Belgium: the Afsluitdijk dam (1932) crosses the IJsselmeer, the Flevoland polder (1950s to 1960s) is shown, and the Benelux borders are modern, although Belgium did not exist in Lannoy's boyhood. The rest is right: a pale-haired boy of about ten in period dress, a star fort drawn with ruler and compasses, no people and no writing on the paper, cold grey northern light, sound hands.

fixes.correction: Nagoji must wear his wrapped rust-red turban exactly as in the neighbouring parapet panels of pages 16 and 17, with long curly black hair and faint grey at the temples showing below it and a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe. Never draw him bare-headed in this scene. Keep his cream tunic sleeves rolled to mid-forearm as on pages 16 and 17, but fold his arms so only the outer backs of both forearms face the camera, clean and unmarked: no brand, scar, tattoo, pattern or discoloured patch on either forearm or near either elbow. Keep everything else that worked: the same sunset laterite bastion with the cannon embrasure, the small sailing boats on the inlet and palms beyond; Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals with his hand on the parapet, turning back from the water to speak; Nagoji facing him squarely with arms folded; and open sky above both men for the lettering. Keep both lower corners as plain, low-detail stone floor and parapet shadow with no crates, barrels or coiled rope, so the storm inset can sit there.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) breaks continuity inside a continuous scene. Nagoji is drawn bare-headed, but the chapter 16 bible row (commander sheet: rust-red turban) and every neighbouring parapet panel (16.1, 16.3, 16.4, 17.1, 17.2, 17.4) show him in the rust-red turban, so he would lose it for one panel and get it back in 18.3. His forearm marks are also wrong. With his arms folded, a large pinkish swirled patch sits on the OUTER left forearm near the elbow, not a small patch a hand's width above the wrist on the inner forearm. A reddish scar line is also drawn on his RIGHT forearm. What works: Lannoy matches his sheet (white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals, pale hair with black ribbon, hand on the parapet, turning from the water to speak). Nagoji's face is right (thick curled moustache, clean chin, faint grey, gold stud). The sunset bastion, the inlet and boats, and the open sky for four lettering areas are all good. The lower-left corner has crates, a barrel and coiled rope rather than plain space for the inset.

fixes.correction: Keep the dusk scene below the fort wall exactly as composed: torches running for the ditch, the two barking dogs, a man blowing a whistle, muskets being snatched up, the empty scrub and rocks beyond, and the open upper sky left clear for the caption. Dress every sentry as in the next panel (19.2): white or off-white turbans with at most a thin red band, a white tunic and a red waist sash. No rust-red, maroon or dark-red turban appears on anyone, so no sentry can be mistaken for Nagoji, who is NOT in this panel. Make the nearest foreground sentry clearly a different man from Nagoji: white turban, no talwar, musket in hand. All muskets are 1740s flintlocks with a visible flint cock and frizzen on the lock plate and a wooden ramrod under the barrel. No levers, hinged breech blocks, percussion caps or modern sights.
fixes.issues: The beat is there (sentries scattering below the wall, muskets, two barking dogs, a man blowing a whistle, torches running for the ditch, empty scrub, clear sky for the caption). The problem is the biggest figure in the frame, the foreground sentry. He wears a dark rust-red/maroon turban, a cream tunic and a red sash, which are Nagoji's signature colours, and the whistle-blower is dressed the same way. Both are bearded. Coming straight after 18.5, the foreground man reads as a bearded Nagoji, who should not be in this panel and must be clean-chinned. The sentries also don't match 19.2, where the same sentries wear white turbans with a red band. The foreground musket's lock is unclear: there is no clear flint cock or frizzen, and a side bar looks like a later breech-loader's lever.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition, guardroom, lamplight and all three figures unchanged: Ramayyan seated with his palm-leaf bundles and stylus, Lannoy apart in his white coat and mundu turning the chipped parapet stone, Nagoji standing by the door with arms folded. Change only Nagoji's sleeves. His cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists and stay down, so no forearm skin shows and NO scar, brand, slash, cross or mark of any kind is visible on either arm. Keep his rust-red turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, broad red sash and talwar exactly as they are.
fixes.issues: Otherwise strong. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm leaves and stylus, seated by the lamp). Lannoy is in the white coat, mundu and sandals with his pale hair ribboned, apart, turning the chipped stone. Nagoji stands by the door with the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey at the temples, red sash and talwar. There is good dark wall space for three balloons. The failure is Nagoji's bare, crossed forearms: on the LEFT forearm's visible outer face, a white scar runs ACROSS the arm through a horizontal mottled patch. Together they read as a cross-shaped mark. The bible says the scar runs along the forearm from wrist toward elbow, beside a brand on the INNER forearm that is 'not a cross'.

fixes.correction: Keep Nagoji, Lannoy, the pillared hall, the brass lamps, the morning courtyard light and the walking composition exactly as they are. Change only the two Nair guards walking a few paces behind, to match the guards established in panel 19.4. Each carries a long curved Nair sword held point-down in the right hand and a small round black shield with brass bosses on the left arm. There are NO spears, lances or poles anywhere in the panel. Both are bare-chested with NO upper or shoulder cloth, wear only a plain white mundu with no red sash or coloured border, and go barefoot with no sandals. Their hair is in a high Kerala topknot, they have moustaches and scarred forearms, and they wear no sacred thread or forehead marks. Nagoji's talwar keeps the Indian disc-pommel hilt from his sheet, with no tsuba-like guard.
fixes.issues: Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples, unmarked forearms) and Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) are good, leaving the same hall as in 19.4, and the upper hall and courtyard have caption space. The two Nair guards are wrong. They carry SPEARS instead of the swords the script calls for. They also wear a white upper cloth over one shoulder, red waist sashes and sandals. In 19.4, where the script fixes their look for pages 19 to 21, they are bare-chested in plain white mundus with no sash and carry long curved swords, one with a round shield. Nagoji's talwar hilt also has a disc guard like a Japanese tsuba.

fixes.correction: Pull the camera far back into a true wide shot. The four figures stand small on the southern wall walk in the lower third of the frame, each no taller than about one fifth of the frame height, seen from a distance in profile or three-quarter back view as they look out toward the setting sun. Nagoji reads by his rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash and boots. Lannoy reads by his pale hair and white tunic-coat over a white mundu. The two Nair shadows (bare-chested, topknots, white mundus, a long sword and a round shield each) stand a few paces behind them. Keep the warm last-light palette, the stone bastions, palms, river and hills of 21.1 and this version. Give the whole upper half of the frame to open, softly graded sunset sky with only thin cloud, so three captions can sit there. Show no flag, or only Travancore's silver conch on red, and never a plain white flag.
fixes.issues: Framing does not match the script. 21.2 calls for a wide shot with the men small against the sky. Here Nagoji and Lannoy are a medium walking two-shot filling about two-thirds of the frame height. That nearly repeats 21.1 (same pair, same wall, same dusk, Nairs at left) and loses the page's pull-back before the close. Likenesses, costumes and the Nair shadows (topknots, white mundus, sword and round shield) are otherwise correct. Also: a plain blank white flag on the tower could read as a surrender flag.

fixes.correction: Make the crop with the frame edge, not with the wall. Camera low and close at knee height, with the strip's top edge cutting the soldiers at the waist so no heads or upper bodies appear. Five or six barefoot soldiers in white dhotis march past left to right in step and in neat order. Each figure is whole and continuous and stands entirely in front of the parapet; no wall, coping, lamp or object passes in front of any body. Each carries a flintlock musket at the shoulder in the eighteenth-century manner: the left hand cups the butt at hip height and the stock and barrel rise steeply upward out of the top edge of the frame. The musket is never held low or horizontal across the body. Keep the dusk light, the stone flagstones and the fort wall behind them. Leave the left quarter of the strip as plain, shadowed parapet wall and flagstone with no figure in it, for the two captions.
fixes.issues: The marching soldiers are sliced off at the waist by the parapet coping. Their legs are in front of the wall, yet the wall top passes in front of their upper bodies, which is spatially impossible. The muskets are carried low across the body in the hand, not shouldered as the script asks. The bare feet, dhotis, dusk light and fort setting are right.
